correctness.rationale: Independence-number recursion alpha(s)=max(alpha(s without lowest bit),1+alpha(s without closed neighborhood of lowest bit)) is exact on *all* 2^(3n) subsets for both specified finite graphs. Each k-face is exactly one with alpha(s)<k; the deterministic greedy element-toggle matching pairs codimension-one incident faces, leaving one critical 0-cell and b critical cells only in dimension 2k−3 (or only critical vertex). Crucially, an independent C++17 reconstruction (different memory and graph implementation from the supplied Python verifier) enumerated the full face posets for k=4,5,6,7,8 on n=5 and k=4..9 on n=6, reversed each matched incidence, and fully topologically sorted every oriented Hasse digraph, with visited count exactly total face count in each case. Example: n5 k5 12826 faces, 67 critical 7-cells; n6 k5 38417 faces, 206 critical 7-cells; n6 k8 249408 faces, 33 critical 13-cells. All 11 nontrivial/high boundary cases matched the submitted multiplicities; the audited original code separately handles known k2,3 and high trivial k. A finite discrete Morse matching is exhaustive for the *two finite grids* and Forman’s homotopy theorem upgrades the critically homogeneous CW complexes to integral sphere wedges. It is not extrapolated to arbitrary strip length.
residual_risks: Finite numerical corroboration is explicitly distinguished from the quantified analytic proof or exhaustive finite certificate.

Example 10 already shows a binomial failure at a different grid and the top-k maximal-independent-set result is old, so the audited novelty is not first failure anywhere. Theorem 1 and the general k≥4 corner-gluing challenge remain a conjectural direction in that paper, and the inspected statements do not determine the specific 3×5/3×6 full k≥4 homotopy spectra. Chandrakar et al grid total-cut work gives total 3-cut for width three, not higher k. Published Resultary search produced a general k3 bipartite graph theorem and unrelated finite grids, not the new parameters.

value.rationale: The two adjacent width-three rectangular grids are the first small substantial corner-gluing test cases beyond established low-k theory, showing exact homotopy types (not just ranks) through the full parameter range and pinpointing initial low-parameter binomial-count breakdown. This finite census answers sharply motivated cases of an explicit open structural wedge-conjecture without pretending to prove an infinite grid family; the complete integral certificate is independently useful for future generalizations.
residual_risks: Value assessment is mathematical usefulness of the precise new claim, not an assertion of broad downstream impact or publication prestige.

final_claim: For G_n=P_3□P_n with n=5 and 6, the complexes R_k(G_n)={W:alpha(G_n[W])<k} have complete *integral homotopy* types wedge^{b_nk} S^{2k-3} or contractible. For n=5, b at k=2..7 is (8,28,56,67,42,7) and k≥8 contractible; n=6, b at k=2..9 is (10,45,120,206,225,139,33,1) and k≥10 contractible. The binomial multiplicity holds through k=4 but fails already at k=5: 67 instead of 70 and 206 instead of 210. New higher k cases and exact finite Morse certificates are the substance; k=2,3 and top maximal-independent-set cases are prior/boundary facts.
limitations: Only two finite grids P3×P5 and P3×P6; no general width-three strip theorem. k=2,3 old; the last independent-set thresholds are known in Filakovský. Integral homotopy conclusion follows from complete acyclic matching and Morse CW theorem, not just Euler characteristics.
